documents.title: The note is in your handwriting
documents.body: It says: Leave earlier on Thursday. Nothing else. The crumbs settle into a date three weeks from now, and the stamp on the crust reads Advice Issued, Not Binding.

documents.title: The message goes under the butter
documents.body: The words soften and disappear. The toaster clicks once, politely, and raises a second slice that says only Understood. Somewhere ahead of you, a version of you stops drafting advice.

documents.title: A sentence resumes mid-word
documents.body: A voice finishes saying because, then pauses, surprised that anyone is still there. It explains the rest in under a minute. It was not about you, and it was never as bad as it sounded.

documents.title: The exchange goes quiet
documents.body: Two hundred conversations stop on the same word. In the silence, the operator's chair turns slightly toward you, and a card drops from the ledger: Service suspended at the caller's request.

documents.title: The blank jack rings back
documents.body: The unlabelled jack connects to a conversation that has not happened yet. You hear yourself say anyway, someone laughs, and the line holds its breath, waiting for the rest.

documents.title: An afternoon comes back indoors
documents.body: Steam gathers under the ceiling into a low, patient drizzle. A coat is drying by a door that is not there, and a voice asks whether you are staying for a second cup. You are counted.

documents.title: The kettle stays cold
documents.body: Nothing boils. For a while afterwards, your visitors arrive in perfectly ordinary weather and leave before the rain, and none of them can say later what the sky was doing while you talked.

draftDocument.title: The Toaster That Prints Notes From Your Future Self
draftDocument.accessionNote: Recovered from the staff kitchen of the Municipal Bureau of Advance Notice.
draftDocument.summary: A two-slot municipal toaster browns short messages onto each slice, written and signed by whoever you will be a year from now. Citizens were advised to read before buttering, and never to reply.
draftDocument.artifactLabel: The browning dial is marked in weeks rather than shades. The crumb tray still holds three unread slices, each stamped with an official date of issue.
draftDocument.visualDescription: A rounded chrome toaster sits on a folded tea towel. Two slices stand half-risen in its slots, darkened with small handwriting, and its browning dial is marked in weeks instead of shades.

draftDocument.title: The Switchboard for Conversations That Ended Too Soon
draftDocument.accessionNote: Removed intact from the night exchange at Counterfactual Relay Station Four.
draftDocument.summary: An operator's switchboard once routed calls to conversations that had ended mid-sentence, reconnecting both parties at the exact word where they stopped. Operators wore two headsets and were trained never to finish anyone's sentence for them.
draftDocument.artifactLabel: Nearly every jack is labelled with the last word spoken before a line went quiet: because, anyway, actually, wait. One cord is still plugged in, and its lamp has not gone out.
draftDocument.visualDescription: A wooden operator's switchboard stands upright, its face covered in rows of brass jacks with tiny word labels, one left blank. Braided cords hang in loops below, and a small lamp glows beside the one connected cord.

image.alt: Blueprint drawing of an upright switchboard with rows of labelled jacks and looped cords, and a detail view of a single lit jack labelled WAIT.

choices.label: Answer the line that is still lit
Plug a cord into the blank jack

draftDocument.title: The Kettle That Brews the Weather of Past Visits
draftDocument.accessionNote: Donated by a lodging house that kept its guest book in steam instead of ink.
draftDocument.summary: An enamel kettle records the weather outside each time a visitor was offered tea. When boiled, it releases a small cloud of that afternoon into the room, along with the smell of wet coats drying by the door.
draftDocument.artifactLabel: The spout is lightly frosted, though the kettle has not been cold in years. Painted around the base are small tallies, one for every guest who stayed for a second cup.
draftDocument.visualDescription: A pale blue enamel kettle sits on a cast-iron trivet. A thin curl of grey cloud hangs above its spout, faint frost rims the spout's edge, and rows of small painted tally marks circle its base.
